summary: Defines extensions to the vCard data format for contact information used in the ICANN operational profile for the Registration Data Access Protocol (RDAP). A property and a parameter are added to RDAP responses consistent with ICANN policy. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Extra fields on a digital contact card, used when looking up who owns a domain, to meet rules set by ICANN.

subtitle: New contact fields for domain registry data according to ICANN policy

tldr.problem: ICANN policy requires contact information in domain registry lookups to include email or web contact URIs and ISO 3166 country codes, but the standard vCard format does not have fields for these.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8605 adds two extensions to vCard: a CONTACT-URI property to hold email or web form URIs, and a CC parameter on the address property to specify the ISO 3166 two-letter country code.
tldr.outcome: Domain registries can now include ICANN-compliant contact information in RDAP responses without violating vCard structure.

facts.label: New property
facts.value: CONTACT-URI (holds email or web form URIs)

today: RFC 8605 is an Informational specification and is not obsoleted. ICANN operational profiles for RDAP use these extensions, and they are registered in the IANA vCard registries.

sections.title: ICANN Requirements for Contact Data
sections.content:
The Temporary Specification for gTLD Registration Data published by ICANN in 2018 sets requirements for how generic top-level domain registries must expose contact information. The Registration Data Access Protocol (RDAP) returns entity objects representing Registrant, Admin, and Tech contacts using the vCard format as defined in RFC 6350.

ICANN policy requires that contact information include either an email address or a web form URI for reaching the contact, and that country information use ISO 3166 two-letter country codes rather than country names. The base vCard specification did not support these requirements, so RFC 8605 adds them as extensions.
sections.eli5: When someone looks up a domain, they get a contact card. The new rules say the card must show how to reach the contact (email or form) and use short country codes (like US, CA) instead of full names.

sections.title: The CONTACT-URI Property
sections.content:
The new CONTACT-URI property holds a URI (such as a mailto or https URL) for contacting the registrant, admin, or tech contact. It can be a mailto: URI, an http: URI pointing to a web form, or an https: URI for secure web forms. At least one CONTACT-URI property MUST be provided.

The property supports the PREF parameter to indicate which contact method is preferred if multiple CONTACT-URI properties are present. Multiple CONTACT-URI properties MAY be used to list alternative contact methods. Example: CONTACT-URI;PREF=1:mailto:contact@example.com or CONTACT-URI:https://contact.example.com.
sections.eli5: Instead of showing an email address directly, the contact field can point to an email link or a form on a website. You can list more than one option and say which is preferred.

sections.title: The CC Parameter for Country Codes
sections.content:
The new CC parameter extends the vCard ADR (address) property. It carries an ISO 3166 two-letter country code (such as US, GB, or JP) to identify the country without using a country name. This meets ICANN requirements for unambiguous, standardized country identification.

The CC parameter is formatted as two uppercase letters. Example: ADR;TYPE=work;CC=US:;;54321 Oak St;Reston;VA;20190;USA. The parameter is simply added to the existing ADR property; it does not change the vCard structure.
sections.eli5: On the address part of the contact card, instead of writing "United States", you just add a CC=US label. It is the same as on passports.

sections.title: Usage in RDAP Responses
sections.content:
When an RDAP server returns entity objects for domain contact information, it now includes the CONTACT-URI property for each contact method (email or web form). The IANA registries have been updated to recognize both the CONTACT-URI property (added to the vCard Properties registry) and the CC parameter (added to the vCard Parameters registry).

The extensions are optional additions to vCard. Clients that do not understand CONTACT-URI or CC simply ignore these fields, while compliant RDAP clients parse them to provide the contact information that ICANN requires. The changes are backward compatible.
sections.eli5: Servers that look up domain owners can now include the contact link and country code. Old software will still work; it just will not see the new fields.
